| IrishGenealogy.ie | Civil registration births, marriages, deaths from 1864; Church of Ireland and some Presbyterian registers | Free |
| National Archives of Ireland (census.nationalarchives.ie / NAI) | 1901 and 1911 census (free, fully indexed); Tithe Applotment Books; school records | Free |
| AskAboutIreland.ie | Griffith's Primary Valuation (free, fully indexed) | Free |
| PRONI (proni.gov.uk) | Church registers on microfilm; estate papers; Poor Law Union records; civil registration for Northern Ireland | Free online index; some images require in-person visit |
| NLI (registers.nli.ie) | Roman Catholic parish registers (microfilm images, free, browse-by-parish) | Free |
| FindMyPast | Tithe Applotment Books; some Irish census substitutes; British newspaper archive | Subscription |
| Ancestry | Griffith's Valuation; passenger lists; some Irish church records | Subscription |
| FamilySearch | Some Irish church records and civil registration indexes | Free |

**Coverage of this survey:** The place-resolution and collections-search tools returned zero results for all Ireland/Antrim-related place names in this session. The online repositories listed above are drawn from Irish genealogical practice generally; no specific collection IDs, record counts, or DGS (film) numbers were returned by tool output. Researchers should search the FamilySearch Catalog directly for "Billy, Antrim" and "County Antrim" to identify specific microfilmed volumes and their current digitization status.

**Note on the FamilySearch Catalog:** The catalog_search tool could not be run in this session because no standardPlace was successfully resolved. The FamilySearch Catalog (familysearch.org/catalog) should be searched directly under "Ballylinny, Billy, County Antrim" and "County Antrim, Ireland" to find specific film/DGS holdings.

### Physical repositories

| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| PRONI, Belfast (proni.gov.uk) | Church registers (microfilm and originals); estate papers; Poor Law Union records; civil registration for Northern Ireland; census substitutes | Reading room; appointment recommended; some indexes free online |
| National Archives of Ireland, Dublin (nationalarchives.ie) | Pre-1922 records including will abstracts; census fragments; valuation records; school records | Reading room; online catalog |
| General Register Office, Roscommon | Original civil registration records from 1845/1864 | Written request; some indexes online |
| Representative Church Body Library, Dublin (ireland.anglican.org/rcb) | Church of Ireland registers and vestry records | Reading room by appointment |
| Presbyterian Historical Society, Belfast | Presbyterian session records and registers | Reading room by appointment |
| Diocese of Down and Connor Archives | Roman Catholic registers and diocesan records | Contact diocese |
| British Library / The National Archives, Kew | British Army records; some plantation-era Irish records | Reading room / online (Discovery catalogue) |
| Ballymoney Library (North Eastern Education and Library Board) | Local newspapers; local history collections | In-person |

---

## Records NOT online

- **Pre-1864 civil vital records:** None exist; the entire pre-civil-registration period for Billy parish relies on church registers, many of which are at PRONI in microfilm or original form and not fully indexed online.
- **Estate papers for Billy parish landlords:** Held physically at PRONI; not fully digitized or indexed online.
- **Poor Law Union (Ballymoney) workhouse records:** Held at PRONI; access is largely in-person.
- **Presbyterian session minutes:** Generally not indexed online; held at PRONI or the Presbyterian Historical Society.
- **Vestry minutes (Church of Ireland):** At PRONI; not generally available online in searchable form.
- **Pre-1820 passenger lists:** Highly fragmentary; no comprehensive database exists. Newspaper notices are the main surviving source.
- **Registry of Deeds (Dublin) originals:** Indexed online at some subscription sites, but original deed images require in-person or mail access to the Registry of Deeds, Dublin.

---

## Known record losses

The most significant record loss affecting Billy parish research is the **destruction of the Public Record Office of Ireland (PROI) in Dublin in June 1922** during the Four Courts fire in the Irish Civil War. This fire destroyed:

- The majority of Irish **census returns for 1821, 1831, 1841, and 1851**. No comprehensive substitute census survives for County Antrim (including Billy parish) for those years, making Griffith's Valuation and the Tithe Applotment Books critically important.
- Most pre-1858 **will books and administration bonds** from the ecclesiastical probate courts, including those of the Consistorial Court of Down and Connor relevant to Billy parish.

No tool result in this session confirmed the specific fate of any individual Billy parish church register. Researchers should confirm directly with PRONI and the RCB Library which specific registers for Billy parish churches survive, are on microfilm, and whether any gaps exist for the 1780–1870 period.

The **1861 and 1871 census returns** for all of Ireland were ordered destroyed by government; this is not a fire loss but a deliberate destruction.

---

## Research tips

### Naming conventions

The following comes directly from the FamilySearch Wiki page **"Ireland Naming Customs"** (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Naming_Customs):

- Irish surnames of Gaelic origin were often anglicized under English rule. The prefixes *Mac* (son of) and *O* (grandson/descendant of) became fixed parts of hereditary surnames, then were frequently dropped or restored over time — so the same family may appear as O'Flynn, Flynn, and Flinn across different records and years.
- Spelling was not standardized; a single family's surname may be recorded several ways within one parish register.
- Irish given names are also Gaelic in origin and were affected by anglicization; for example, Darby, Dermot, and Jeremiah are all variations of the same name.
- Some given names were used for both males and females (e.g. Florence, Sydney, Evelyn).
- A **traditional naming pattern** was commonly followed by Irish parents until the later 19th century:
  - First son: usually named for the father's father
  - Second son: usually named for the mother's father
  - Third son: usually named for the father
  - Fourth son: usually named for the father's eldest brother
  - First daughter: usually named for the mother's mother
  - Second daughter: usually named for the father's mother
  - Third daughter: usually named for the mother
- The FamilySearch Wiki page notes explicitly: "The pattern is a clue, not a rule — it was not universally followed, and a broken pattern is not evidence of non-identity."

### Research sequence recommended for Billy parish, 1780–1870

1. **Start with Griffith's Valuation (c. 1856–1858)** at AskAboutIreland.ie — free, fully indexed, gives townland-level location of every household head in Billy parish at mid-century. Note the townland for subsequent record searches.
2. **Cross to the Tithe Applotment Books (c. 1823–1837)** at the NAI or FindMyPast — identifies the same families two to three decades earlier and confirms landholder status.
3. **Search church registers** via PRONI and IrishGenealogy.ie. Identify which congregation served your family's townland; do not assume the Church of Ireland register is the right one — in heavily Presbyterian north Antrim, many families will appear only in Presbyterian registers.
4. **Search the 1901 and 1911 censuses** (census.nationalarchives.ie) to anchor the family at the end of the period and work backward.
5. **Check the 1796 Flax Growers' List** (available on Ancestry and some free databases) for the earliest portion of the target period — it names those who received spinning wheels, useful for identifying households before the Tithe Books.
6. **Search passenger lists** (FamilySearch, Ancestry) for emigrant family members, particularly after 1845. The 1851 Griffith's household combined with the Tithe Books can reveal who was present before famine emigration.
7. **Search PRONI estate papers** for the relevant landlord estate if the family was a tenant — rental lists, lease books, and correspondence can name individual tenants by townland.
8. **Search surviving probate abstracts** at NAI and PRONI (Sir William Betham's abstracts; the printed Will Calendars from 1858) for any testators in the family.

### Cross-border and adjoining jurisdictions

Billy parish in north County Antrim borders other County Antrim civil parishes. Families near parish boundaries may have worshipped — and generated records — in adjacent parishes. County Londonderry (Derry) lies to the west of County Antrim; families in the western townlands of Billy parish may have connections to Londonderry-side records. The FamilySearch Wiki page for County Antrim Genealogy was not retrievable in this session, so the specific neighbouring parishes are not confirmed from tool output. Researchers should consult the townland and civil parish boundary maps (available at townlands.ie) to identify the relevant adjoining parishes and check their registers as well.

### General Irish research strategy

- In the 1780–1870 period in Ireland, church registers — not civil records — are the primary vital record source for the great majority of the target window. Identifying the correct denomination for a family is therefore the first priority.
- The **absence of a family from Griffith's Valuation** does not mean they did not live in Billy parish — it means they were not landholders (labourers, cottiers, and sub-tenants are often missing).
- The **1922 fire is not a total loss** — many indexes, abstracts, transcripts, and microfilm copies made before 1922 survive. Always check for secondary copies before concluding a record is gone.
- When searching databases, try surname variants systematically (e.g., O'Flynn / Flynn / Flinn) as noted in the Naming Customs guidance above.

---

Step 6 did not run — no research.json project file was found in the working directory.

---

Billy civil parish is a small civil parish on the north Antrim coast of Ireland. For the years 1780 to 1870, there are no surviving civil birth, marriage, or death records for most of this window — Irish civil registration did not begin until 1864 for all denominations — so church registers (Presbyterian, Church of Ireland, and Roman Catholic) held at the Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI) in Belfast and the National Library of Ireland are the primary vital sources. The four surviving Irish census returns for this period were destroyed in 1922 and by government order, making the Tithe Applotment Books of the 1820s–1830s and Griffith's Primary Valuation of the 1850s (both free online) the essential substitutes for placing families in specific townlands. The most important warning for this area is that north Antrim was heavily Presbyterian, so researchers must identify which denomination served their family's townland before searching registers, and must not rely solely on Church of Ireland records.

The recommended next step is to search Griffith's Valuation and the Tithe Applotment Books to establish the townland location of your family, then identify the relevant church congregation and confirm whether its registers survive at PRONI before ordering images or planning a visit.

**Key jurisdictional context:**

- Annual tax lists, court minute books, most Catholic parish registers, coal company employment rolls
- **Contact:** Schuylkill County Courthouse, Schuylkill County Historical Society, Diocese of Allentown, or Hagley Museum and Library

**Recommended next step:** Build a research plan targeting Catholic church registers and post-1850 census enumerations.

# Locality Guide: Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania (1840-1880)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** 1811 from Berks and Northampton Counties
- **County seat / administrative center:** Pottsville
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Commonwealth of Pennsylvania
- **Population during period:** Population data was not returned by the place_population tool for this place; consult published Pennsylvania census compilations for county-level figures.
- **Economy:** Anthracite coal mining was the dominant industry throughout the 1840-1880 period, supported by iron manufacturing and agriculture in the northern and eastern townships. The coal trade drew large numbers of immigrant laborers.
- **Ethnic composition:** Significant Irish, Welsh, English, and German immigrant communities arrived primarily from the 1840s onward, drawn by coal mining work. Earlier settlers were predominantly of German and Scots-Irish descent.
- **Religious denominations:** Roman Catholic (Irish and later immigrant miners), Welsh Congregational and Methodist, German Lutheran and Reformed, Episcopal/Anglican, Presbyterian, and various Protestant evangelical denominations.
- **Key historical events:** Rapid expansion of the anthracite coalfields from the 1840s; the Molly Maguires labor conflict of the 1870s; major railroad development linking the county to Philadelphia and New York markets.

## Boundary changes
- Schuylkill County was formed in 1811 from portions of Berks and Northampton Counties. Its boundaries were stable throughout the 1840-1880 target period.
- Records for events before 1811 are held under Berks County (for the southern portion) or Northampton County (for the northern portion).
- `place_search_all` returned no additional historical representations, confirming the county has existed under a single jurisdiction since 1811.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Pennsylvania did not enact statewide civil registration of births, marriages, or deaths during the 1840-1880 period. A statewide system was not required until 1906. The FamilySearch wiki pages for Pennsylvania Vital Records did not return substantive content in this survey (all resolved to a generic page); researchers should consult the Pennsylvania State Archives directly for any earlier local or county-level registration experiments.
- **What exists for 1840-1880:** No statewide civil birth or death registration covers this window. County-level marriage registers began in Pennsylvania in 1885 — after the close of the target period. For 1840-1880 marriages, the primary documentary sources are church registers and compiled marriage indexes.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch collections covering marriages include:
  - *Pennsylvania, Civil Marriages, 1677-1950* (collection 1571957): 312,045 records, 156,023 images — https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1571957
  - *Pennsylvania, Compiled Marriages, 1700-1900* (collection 1502909): 198,765 records, no images — https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1502909
  - *Pennsylvania, County Marriages, 1885-1950* (collection 1921317): 524,189 records — begins after the target period, but covers events for individuals who married after 1885 and may be relevant for collateral research.
- **Gaps:** No indexed civil birth or death records for 1840-1880. Death certificates begin in 1906 (collection 2255317, 4.2 million indexed records — https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2255317) but are outside the target window.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church baptismal, marriage, and burial registers are the primary vital record source for this period (see Church Records below). Mortality schedules from the 1850, 1860, 1870, and 1880 federal censuses record deaths in the year preceding each census and are a critical substitute for death registration.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Roman Catholic, German Lutheran, German Reformed, Welsh Congregational and Methodist, Episcopal, Presbyterian, and Methodist Episcopal congregations are known to have been active in Schuylkill County during this period, reflecting the county's immigrant mining population.
- **Record types:** Baptisms/christenings, marriages, burials, and confirmations. German Lutheran and Reformed registers may include family registers (Familienbücher).
- **Where held:** FamilySearch holds a digitized church records volume (imageGroupNumber 007936751) covering Schuylkill County, 1842-1895, 187 images. This volume is **browse-only** (0% name-indexed, not full-text searchable) and includes both English and German-language entries. Researchers must browse image by image and must be able to read German script for German-language registers.
- **FamilySearch collection:** *Pennsylvania, Schuylkill County Church Records* (collection SYNTH-PA-CHURCH, 1708-1985): 1,245,830 records, 982,415 persons, 607,220 images — https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/SYNTH-PA-CHURCH. This is the most substantive indexed church record collection returned for this county.
- **Additional access:** The Pennsylvania State Archives, diocesan archives (Diocese of Allentown for Catholic records; Lutheran and Reformed synodal archives), and local historical societies hold original parish registers not fully represented in FamilySearch.
- **Language:** A significant portion of church records are in German (Lutheran and Reformed congregations). Latin may appear in pre-1870 Catholic sacramental registers.

### Census records
- **Federal census:** Decennial enumerations for 1840, 1850, 1860, 1870, and 1880 all cover Schuylkill County. The 1840 census lists heads of household only. From 1850 onward, all household members are named. The 1880 census is the first to state the relationship of each person to the head of household.
- **Mortality schedules:** The 1850, 1860, 1870, and 1880 mortality schedules record deaths in the prior year and are a critical substitute for death registration in this period.
- **State census:** Pennsylvania did not conduct regular state-level censuses during 1840-1880.
- **Access:** Federal census collections for Pennsylvania are indexed and available on FamilySearch (free) and Ancestry (subscription). The 1850 Schuylkill County census is confirmed indexed on both platforms (see project log). The 1880 census is fully indexed on FamilySearch. The 1890 federal census was largely destroyed by fire and is not available for this county.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, letters of administration, guardianships, inventories, and estate distributions filed at the Schuylkill County Orphans' Court and Court of Common Pleas.
- **Testate vs. intestate:** Search wills first for property-owning individuals; for those dying intestate (no will), look for letters of administration in the administration dockets.
- **Date range:** From county formation in 1811. The digitized FamilySearch probate volume (007936749) covers 1851-1930, 412 images.
- **Digitization level:** **Browse-only images.** The probate volume is 0% name-indexed and not full-text searchable. The broader FamilySearch collection *Pennsylvania, Probate Records, 1683-1994* (collection 1999196) holds 3,200,560 images with no indexed records — https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1999196. All probate materials must be browsed image by image or consulted in person.
- **Where held:** Originals at the Schuylkill County Courthouse, Pottsville. Pennsylvania State Archives holds some older probate series.

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds (Pennsylvania is a state-land state; the federal rectangular survey system does not apply).
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** Original land grants were issued under the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania. The Pennsylvania State Archives holds the original warrant and patent records. County deed books, held at the Schuylkill County Recorder of Deeds, document subsequent transfers.
- **Types:** Deeds, mortgages, warrants, patents, and tax records.
- **Date range:** County deed records from 1811. The digitized deed records volume (007936752) covers 1815-1900, 543 images, and is 22% name-indexed — a partial index covering a portion of the volume. The remainder must be browsed.
- **Where held:** Schuylkill County Recorder of Deeds (Pottsville) for deed books. Pennsylvania State Archives for warrants and patents. FamilySearch volume 007936752 provides partial online access.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Mexican-American War (1846-1848), American Civil War (1861-1865).
- **Record types:** Union service records and pension files at NARA (Record Group 94 for service records; RG 15 for pension files). Bounty land warrants were available to veterans of pre-Civil War service. Pennsylvania adjutant general records and regimental histories are at the Pennsylvania State Archives. Civil War draft registration records (1863) are at NARA.
- **Where held:** NARA (Washington, D.C. / St. Louis). Pennsylvania State Archives (Harrisburg). Indexed Civil War pension and service records are available on Fold3 (subscription) and partially on FamilySearch and Ancestry.

### Cemetery records
- **Major cemeteries:** Numerous church and municipal cemeteries exist throughout Schuylkill County, reflecting the county's diverse denominational landscape. Catholic, Lutheran, Reformed, Methodist, and nondenominational cemeteries serve communities across the mining patches and borough seats.
- **Online coverage:** Find A Grave (findagrave.com) and BillionGraves (billiongraves.com) index many Schuylkill County cemetery inscriptions; coverage is volunteer-driven and incomplete.
- **Physical records:** Sexton records and burial registers are held at individual churches and cemeteries; some have been deposited with the Schuylkill County Historical Society.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** The *Miners' Journal* (Pottsville), founded 1825, is the county's most significant newspaper for this period and published continuously through and beyond 1840-1880. Other local papers existed in borough centers.
- **Where held:** The *Miners' Journal* is microfilmed and held by the Library of Congress, the Pennsylvania State Library, and the Schuylkill County Historical Society. Some issues may be available through Chronicling America (chroniclingamerica.loc.gov) or newspaper archives databases.
- **Content value:** Obituaries (may name birthplace and survivors), marriage notices, legal notices (estate settlements, sheriff sales, naturalizations), and community news are all genealogically relevant.

### Immigration and emigration records
- **Relevant ports:** Philadelphia (primary port of entry for Irish, German, and Welsh immigrants to Schuylkill County) and New York (Castle Garden, 1855-1890; Ellis Island, after 1892 — post-period).
- **Record types:** Passenger arrival manifests (Philadelphia and New York); naturalization declarations and petitions filed in Schuylkill County courts; alien registrations.
- **Naturalization:** A digitized naturalization records volume (007936750, 1849-1915, 298 images) exists for Schuylkill County on FamilySearch and is **browse-only** (0% name-indexed, not full-text searchable). Pre-1906 declarations of intention and petitions could be filed in any court of record — including local Common Pleas courts as well as federal courts. Search both Schuylkill County court records and Philadelphia-area federal court records.
- **Where held:** Passenger lists at NARA (digitized on Ancestry and FamilySearch for the Philadelphia series). Naturalization records at the Schuylkill County Courthouse and NARA regional facilities.
- **Content note:** Passenger lists record every person aboard, including infants and young children traveling with parents. Examine the full manifest for all family members when researching an immigrant family.

### Tax records
- **Types:** County property (real estate) tax and personal property tax lists were compiled annually at the township and borough level.
- **Date range:** From county formation in 1811; annual lists throughout 1840-1880.
- **Where held:** Schuylkill County Historical Society and Pennsylvania State Archives hold tax lists. The Ancestry collection *Pennsylvania, U.S., Tax and Exoneration Lists, 1768-1801* (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/7667/) predates the target period but establishes earlier family property patterns.
- **Substitute value:** Annual tax lists are an invaluable substitute for the intercensal years and for locating individuals between census enumerations. They can confirm continued residence and property ownership year by year.

### Other record types
- **Occupational records:** Coal mining employment records from the large coal companies (Reading Coal & Iron, Philadelphia & Reading Coal & Iron Company, and others) may document miners by name. These are largely held by corporate successors or have been deposited with the Hagley Museum and Library (Wilmington, Delaware).
- **Court records:** Schuylkill County Court of Common Pleas minutes record civil suits, criminal cases, road orders, and other county business that names ordinary residents. These are held at the Schuylkill County Courthouse.
- **School records:** Township school records from this period are scattered; some are held by the Schuylkill County Historical Society.
- **Organizational records:** The Ancient Order of Hibernians and other Irish fraternal organizations were active in the coal region; membership records may survive at state or national headquarters.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Church Records 1708-1985 (SYNTH-PA-CHURCH, 1.2M records); Probate Records 1683-1994 (1999196, 3.2M images, browse-only); Civil Marriages 1677-1950 (1571957); Compiled Marriages 1700-1900 (1502909); County Marriages 1885-1950 (1921317); Death Certificates 1906-1968 (2255317); digitized volumes: deed records (007936752, 22% indexed), church records (007936751, browse-only), probate (007936749, browse-only), naturalization (007936750, browse-only), marriage (007936753, browse-only) | Free |
| Ancestry | 1850 United States Federal Census - Schuylkill County (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1276/); Pennsylvania Tax and Exoneration Lists 1768-1801 (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/7667/) | Subscription |

**Coverage of this survey:** 5 digitized volumes matched this place and period in volume_search; all 5 are detailed above. This is the complete first-page result set (totalResults: 5, no nextPageToken returned).

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Schuylkill County Courthouse, Pottsville | Deed books, probate files, court minutes, naturalization records, marriage registers (from 1885) | In-person; some records accessible via mail request |
| Schuylkill County Historical Society, Pottsville | Tax lists, cemetery records, local histories, newspaper microfilm, manuscripts | In-person; contact for hours |
| Pennsylvania State Archives, Harrisburg | Land warrants and patents, military records, state agency records, some church records | In-person and online finding aids (phmc.pa.gov) |
| NARA Mid-Atlantic Region, Philadelphia | Federal census originals, passenger lists, naturalization records from federal courts, Civil War records | In-person and online request |
| Diocese of Allentown Archives | Catholic parish registers for Schuylkill County parishes | Contact archives for access |
| Hagley Museum and Library, Wilmington, DE | Coal company employment and corporate records | In-person; contact for access |
| Library of Congress / Pennsylvania State Library | Miners' Journal microfilm | In-person; some digitized via Chronicling America |

## Records NOT online
- Annual township and borough tax lists (1840-1880) — held physically at Schuylkill County Historical Society and Pennsylvania State Archives; not available in any online index for this period.
- Schuylkill County Court of Common Pleas minute books — physical records at the courthouse; not digitized or indexed online.
- Most Catholic parish registers for individual Schuylkill County parishes — original volumes held by parishes and the Diocese of Allentown; not fully represented in FamilySearch.
- Coal company employment records — held by Hagley Museum and Library and corporate successors; not searchable online.
- School records and organizational records — largely physical, scattered among local repositories.
- Naturalization records (volume 007936750) — digitized on FamilySearch but 0% indexed; must be browsed image by image.
- Probate records (volume 007936749 and collection 1999196) — digitized on FamilySearch but 0% indexed; must be browsed image by image.
- Marriage records (volume 007936753) — digitized on FamilySearch but 0% indexed; must be browsed image by image.

## Known record losses
No tool result returned in this survey identifies specific record losses for Schuylkill County. The county courthouse and historical repositories appear to hold substantial original records for the 1840-1880 period. Researchers should contact the Schuylkill County Courthouse and Historical Society directly to confirm the completeness of specific series before assuming a record does not exist.

## Research tips
- **The 1840-1880 target period predates Pennsylvania's statewide civil registration.** Church records are the primary vital record source for this entire window. Begin with the FamilySearch church records collection (SYNTH-PA-CHURCH) and the browse-only digitized volume (007936751), then contact the relevant denominational archives.
- **For Irish immigrant families** (as with the Flynn research in this project), Catholic baptismal and marriage registers are essential. The Diocese of Allentown holds records for Schuylkill County Catholic parishes. Irish immigrants typically arrived through Philadelphia; search the Philadelphia passenger arrival manifests on Ancestry and FamilySearch.
- **German-language records require language skills.** The digitized church records volume (007936751) includes German-language entries. German Lutheran and Reformed registers commonly use Kurrent or Sütterlin script; use the FamilySearch Paleography resources or a transcription specialist.
- **Coal industry context shapes the record base.** The heavy influx of immigrant miners from the 1840s onward means that church membership records, naturalization filings, and company employment rolls may together provide more information than sparse civil records alone.
- **Use annual tax lists between census years.** Federal census enumerations are ten years apart. Annual township tax lists confirm residence and property ownership in intercensal years and can track a family's movement within the county.
- **Naturalization was a multi-step process.** A miner who immigrated in 1845 might file a declaration of intention (first papers) at the Schuylkill County Court of Common Pleas and then petition for naturalization (second papers) years later — or in a different county or state if he moved. Search both Schuylkill County naturalization volume 007936750 and NARA's naturalization index.
- **Search adjoining counties.** Schuylkill County borders Berks, Lebanon, Dauphin, Northumberland, Columbia, and Carbon Counties. Families near any of these borders may have generated records in the adjoining jurisdiction — particularly for events (marriages, land purchases, naturalizations) that occurred just across the line. The neighboring county details were not confirmed from a returned wiki page for this survey; consult the FamilySearch Schuylkill County Genealogy page directly for the neighboring counties table.
- **Mortality schedules (1850-1880) are essential substitutes** for the absent civil death registration. Each is attached to the corresponding federal census; search these schedules for any family member who died in the year preceding each census.
- **The FamilySearch wiki pages for Pennsylvania-specific record types** (Vital Records, Church Records, Land and Property, Probate, Census, and Naming Customs) all resolved to a generic page in this survey and did not return substantive jurisdiction-specific content. Researchers should visit those pages directly at familysearch.org/en/wiki/ to confirm current guidance.

Bounty land warrants were available to veterans of pre-Civil War service. Pennsylvania adjutant general records and regimental histories are at the Pennsylvania State Archives. Civil War draft registration records (1863) are at NARA.
- **Where held:** NARA (Washington, D.C. / St. Louis). Pennsylvania State Archives (Harrisburg). Indexed Civil War pension and service records are available on Fold3 (subscription) and partially on FamilySearch and Ancestry.

### Cemetery records
- **Major cemeteries:** Numerous church and municipal cemeteries exist throughout Schuylkill County, reflecting the county's diverse denominational landscape. Catholic, Lutheran, Reformed, Methodist, and nondenominational cemeteries serve communities across the mining patches and borough seats.
- **Online coverage:** Find A Grave (findagrave.com) and BillionGraves (billiongraves.com) index many Schuylkill County cemetery inscriptions; coverage is volunteer-driven and incomplete.
- **Physical records:** Sexton records and burial registers are held at individual churches and cemeteries; some have been deposited with the Schuylkill County Historical Society.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** The *Miners' Journal* (Pottsville), founded 1825, is the county's most significant newspaper for this period and published continuously through and beyond 1840-1880. Other local papers existed in borough centers.
- **Where held:** The *Miners' Journal* is microfilmed and held by the Library of Congress, the Pennsylvania State Library, and the Schuylkill County Historical Society. Some issues may be available through Chronicling America (chroniclingamerica.loc.gov) or newspaper archives databases.
- **Content value:** Obituaries (may name birthplace and survivors), marriage notices, legal notices (estate settlements, sheriff sales, naturalizations), and community news are all genealogically relevant.

### Immigration and emigration records
- **Relevant ports:** Philadelphia (primary port of entry for Irish, German, and Welsh immigrants to Schuylkill County) and New York (Castle Garden, 1855-1890; Ellis Island, after 1892 — post-period).
- **Record types:** Passenger arrival manifests (Philadelphia and New York); naturalization declarations and petitions filed in Schuylkill County courts; alien registrations.
- **Naturalization:** A digitized naturalization records volume (007936750, 1849-1915, 298 images) exists for Schuylkill County on FamilySearch and is **browse-only** (0% name-indexed, not full-text searchable). Pre-1906 declarations of intention and petitions could be filed in any court of record — including local Common Pleas courts as well as federal courts. Search both Schuylkill County court records and Philadelphia-area federal court records.
- **Where held:** Passenger lists at NARA (digitized on Ancestry and FamilySearch for the Philadelphia series). Naturalization records at the Schuylkill County Courthouse and NARA regional facilities.
- **Content note:** Passenger lists record every person aboard, including infants and young children traveling with parents. Examine the full manifest for all family members when researching an immigrant family.

### Tax records
- **Types:** County property (real estate) tax and personal property tax lists were compiled annually at the township and borough level.
- **Date range:** From county formation in 1811; annual lists throughout 1840-1880.
- **Where held:** Schuylkill County Historical Society and Pennsylvania State Archives hold tax lists. The Ancestry collection *Pennsylvania, U.S., Tax and Exoneration Lists, 1768-1801* (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/7667/) predates the target period but establishes earlier family property patterns.
- **Substitute value:** Annual tax lists are an invaluable substitute for the intercensal years and for locating individuals between census enumerations. They can confirm continued residence and property ownership year by year.

### Other record types
- **Occupational records:** Coal mining employment records from the large coal companies (Reading Coal & Iron, Philadelphia & Reading Coal & Iron Company, and others) may document miners by name. These are largely held by corporate successors or have been deposited with the Hagley Museum and Library (Wilmington, Delaware).
- **Court records:** Schuylkill County Court of Common Pleas minutes record civil suits, criminal cases, road orders, and other county business that names ordinary residents. These are held at the Schuylkill County Courthouse.
- **School records:** Township school records from this period are scattered; some are held by the Schuylkill County Historical Society.
- **Organizational records:** The Ancient Order of Hibernians and other Irish fraternal organizations were active in the coal region; membership records may survive at state or national headquarters.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Church Records 1708-1985 (SYNTH-PA-CHURCH, 1.2M records); Probate Records 1683-1994 (1999196, 3.2M images, browse-only); Civil Marriages 1677-1950 (1571957); Compiled Marriages 1700-1900 (1502909); County Marriages 1885-1950 (1921317); Death Certificates 1906-1968 (2255317); digitized volumes: deed records (007936752, 22% indexed), church records (007936751, browse-only), probate (007936749, browse-only), naturalization (007936750, browse-only), marriage (007936753, browse-only) | Free |
| Ancestry | 1850 United States Federal Census - Schuylkill County (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1276/); Pennsylvania Tax and Exoneration Lists 1768-1801 (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/7667/) | Subscription |

**Coverage of this survey:** 5 digitized volumes matched this place and period in volume_search; all 5 are detailed above. This is the complete first-page result set (totalResults: 5, no nextPageToken returned).

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Schuylkill County Courthouse, Pottsville | Deed books, probate files, court minutes, naturalization records, marriage registers (from 1885) | In-person; some records accessible via mail request |
| Schuylkill County Historical Society, Pottsville | Tax lists, cemetery records, local histories, newspaper microfilm, manuscripts | In-person; contact for hours |
| Pennsylvania State Archives, Harrisburg | Land warrants and patents, military records, state agency records, some church records | In-person and online finding aids (phmc.pa.gov) |
| NARA Mid-Atlantic Region, Philadelphia | Federal census originals, passenger lists, naturalization records from federal courts, Civil War records | In-person and online request |
| Diocese of Allentown Archives | Catholic parish registers for Schuylkill County parishes | Contact archives for access |
| Hagley Museum and Library, Wilmington, DE | Coal company employment and corporate records | In-person; contact for access |
| Library of Congress / Pennsylvania State Library | Miners' Journal microfilm | In-person; some digitized via Chronicling America |

## Records NOT online
- Annual township and borough tax lists (1840-1880) — held physically at Schuylkill County Historical Society and Pennsylvania State Archives; not available in any online index for this period.
- Schuylkill County Court of Common Pleas minute books — physical records at the courthouse; not digitized or indexed online.
- Most Catholic parish registers for individual Schuylkill County parishes — original volumes held by parishes and the Diocese of Allentown; not fully represented in FamilySearch.
- Coal company employment records — held by Hagley Museum and Library and corporate successors; not searchable online.
- School records and organizational records — largely physical, scattered among local repositories.
- Naturalization records (volume 007936750) — digitized on FamilySearch but 0% indexed; must be browsed image by image.
- Probate records (volume 007936749 and collection 1999196) — digitized on FamilySearch but 0% indexed; must be browsed image by image.
- Marriage records (volume 007936753) — digitized on FamilySearch but 0% indexed; must be browsed image by image.

## Known record losses
No tool result returned in this survey identifies specific record losses for Schuylkill County. The county courthouse and historical repositories appear to hold substantial original records for the 1840-1880 period. Researchers should contact the Schuylkill County Courthouse and Historical Society directly to confirm the completeness of specific series before assuming a record does not exist.

## Research tips
- **The 1840-1880 target period predates Pennsylvania's statewide civil registration.** Church records are the primary vital record source for this entire window. Begin with the FamilySearch church records collection (SYNTH-PA-CHURCH) and the browse-only digitized volume (007936751), then contact the relevant denominational archives.
- **For Irish immigrant families** (as with the Flynn research in this project), Catholic baptismal and marriage registers are essential. The Diocese of Allentown holds records for Schuylkill County Catholic parishes. Irish immigrants typically arrived through Philadelphia; search the Philadelphia passenger arrival manifests on Ancestry and FamilySearch.
- **German-language records require language skills.** The digitized church records volume (007936751) includes German-language entries. German Lutheran and Reformed registers commonly use Kurrent or Sütterlin script; use the FamilySearch Paleography resources or a transcription specialist.
- **Coal industry context shapes the record base.** The heavy influx of immigrant miners from the 1840s onward means that church membership records, naturalization filings, and company employment rolls may together provide more information than sparse civil records alone.
- **Use annual tax lists between census years.** Federal census enumerations are ten years apart. Annual township tax lists confirm residence and property ownership in intercensal years and can track a family's movement within the county.
- **Naturalization was a multi-step process.** A miner who immigrated in 1845 might file a declaration of intention (first papers) at the Schuylkill County Court of Common Pleas and then petition for naturalization (second papers) years later — or in a different county or state if he moved. Search both Schuylkill County naturalization volume 007936750 and NARA's naturalization index.
- **Search adjoining counties.** Schuylkill County borders Berks, Lebanon, Dauphin, Northumberland, Columbia, and Carbon Counties. Families near any of these borders may have generated records in the adjoining jurisdiction — particularly for events (marriages, land purchases, naturalizations) that occurred just across the line. The neighboring county details were not confirmed from a returned wiki page for this survey; consult the FamilySearch Schuylkill County Genealogy page directly for the neighboring counties table.
- **Mortality schedules (1850-1880) are essential substitutes** for the absent civil death registration. Each is attached to the corresponding federal census; search these schedules for any family member who died in the year preceding each census.
- **The FamilySearch wiki pages for Pennsylvania-specific record types** (Vital Records, Church Records, Land and Property, Probate, Census, and Naming Customs) all resolved to a generic page in this survey and did not return substantive jurisdiction-specific content. Researchers should visit those pages directly at familysearch.org/en/wiki/ to confirm current guidance.

output.text_response:
# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (Bushmills Area), 1780–1870

## Jurisdiction Overview

- **Civil parish:** Billy, barony of Cary, County Antrim, Province of Ulster
- **Key settlement:** Bushmills (largest town in the parish)
- **Governing body:** Part of the United Kingdom throughout 1780–1870; County Antrim remained in Northern Ireland after 1921 partition — this determines where records are held today
- **Religious composition:** Predominantly Protestant (Church of Ireland/Anglican and Presbyterian/Ulster-Scots), with a Catholic minority (~40% in 1861 per national figures); the Bushmills area reflects heavy Ulster plantation settlement

---

## The Critical Context: 1922 PROI Fire

The single most important factor shaping record survival is the **1922 fire at the Public Record Office of Ireland (PROI) in Dublin**, which destroyed approximately **two-thirds of Church of Ireland registers** that had been deposited there by law. Whether Billy parish's own Church of Ireland registers survived depends on whether they were ever deposited — confirmed only by checking PRONI and the RCB Library (see below).

---

## Record Types Available

### Church Records *(primary source for 1780–1864, before civil registration)*

**Church of Ireland (Anglican/Episcopal)**
- Records begin 1536 in principle; two-thirds destroyed in 1922
- **Where held:** Surviving registers for County Antrim parishes are split between:
  - **PRONI (Belfast)** — consult the [PRONI Guide to Church Records](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf) to confirm whether Billy parish registers survive and their date range. Also check [Digitised Church Records at PRONI](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni#toc-1)
  - **RCB Library (Dublin)** — Representative Church Body Library, Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14. Their [Parish Register List](https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf) shows what survives; [paid search service](https://store.ireland.anglican.org/genealogy) available
- **Online:** Ffolliott Collection of Church of Ireland baptisms, marriages, and burials at FindMyPast (subscription); some digitised registers at PRONI's online portal (free)
- ⚠️ **Whether Billy parish's registers specifically survived 1922 is unconfirmed** — the PRONI Guide and RCB Library list must be checked first

**Roman Catholic**
- Rural parishes typically did not begin keeping registers until **Catholic Emancipation in 1828**; 1780–1828 gap likely has no Catholic records
- Catholic ecclesiastical parish boundaries differ from the civil parish — confirm which Catholic parish covers the Bushmills-area townlands
- **Where held:** Original registers with the parish; microfilm/digital at NLI and Ancestry
- **Online (free):** [National Library of Ireland Catholic Parish Registers](https://registers.nli.ie/)
- **Online (subscription):** [Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1655–1915](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/61039/) at Ancestry; [Ireland Roman Catholic Parish Marriages](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/ireland-roman-catholic-parish-marriages) at FindMyPast

**Presbyterian**
- Average register start date: **1830**; some north Antrim congregations are earlier
- Heavily relevant for the Bushmills area (strong Ulster-Scots settlement)
- **Where held:** PRONI holds many Presbyterian registers for Northern Ireland
- **Online (subscription):** Ireland Non-Conformist Births, Marriages, and Burials at FindMyPast; [Ulster Historical Foundation](http://www.ancestryireland.com/)

---

### Civil Registration *(limited coverage — post-1864 only within target window)*

| Event | Start date | Coverage |
|---|---|---|
| Non-Catholic marriages | 1 April 1845 | All Ireland |
| All births, marriages, deaths | 1 January 1864 | All Ireland |

- **Where held:** General Register Office Northern Ireland (GRONI) for County Antrim
- **Online (free):** [IrishGenealogy.ie](https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/en/) — note: County Antrim coverage may be limited; check GRONI directly
- For **1780–1845**, church registers are the *only* source for vital events

---

### Census and Census Substitutes

No intact Irish national census survives for the 1780–1870 window. The major substitutes are:

| Record | Dates | Coverage | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Tithe Applotment Books** | 1823–1837 | All landholders liable for tithes (townland level) | [IrishGenealogy.ie](https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/en/) — free |
| **Griffith's Primary Valuation** | 1847–1864 | Every occupier and landholder (townland level); the single most important mid-century survey | [AskAboutIreland.ie](https://www.askaboutireland.ie/griffith-valuation/) — free; also Ancestry |
| **Flax growers' lists** | 1796 | Name source for late 18th century in County Antrim | PRONI / some online |
| **Freeholder / voter lists** | Various | Property-holding men; partial survival | PRONI |

---

### Probate Records

- Before 1858: ecclesiastical probate (Prerogative Court of Armagh for higher-value estates; diocesan court of Connor for smaller ones). **Most original wills destroyed in the 1922 fire.**
- After 1858: civil district probate registries
- **Key substitutes for lost wills:**
  - Betham Genealogical Abstracts (FindMyPast)
  - Thrift Genealogical Abstracts (FindMyPast)
  - Crossle Genealogical Abstracts (FindMyPast)
  - [Ireland, Indexes to Wills, Probate Administration, Marriage Bonds and Licences, 1591–1866](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/62077/) at Ancestry
- **Marriage licence bonds** (document marriages among more affluent families): [Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes, 1623–1866](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3460239) at FamilySearch — **free**

---

### Land and Estate Records

# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (Bushmills Area) (1780–1870)

## Jurisdiction overview

- **Civil parish:** Billy, in the barony of Cary, County Antrim, Province of Ulster
- **Town within the parish:** Bushmills (the largest settlement; noted for its distillery and proximity to the Giant's Causeway)
- **Parent jurisdiction:** County Antrim, Province of Ulster, Ireland (part of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland throughout 1780–1870)
- **Administrative center for county matters:** Belfast / Carrickfergus (county assizes); after 1800, Dublin for national records
- **Population:** No population figures were returned by the place tools for this parish; the FamilySearch place tools returned no match for "Billy, County Antrim" or any narrower/broader Antrim search
- **Economy:** Linen weaving, small-scale agriculture, fishing; the Old Bushmills Distillery is a notable local employer from this period
- **Ethnic/religious composition:** The FamilySearch Wiki page for [Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records) states that in Northern Ireland, the Church of Ireland and the Presbyterian churches were the dominant religions, together accounting for approximately 60% of the population in 1861, while Catholics accounted for approximately 40%. County Antrim is in the historic Ulster plantation region, settled heavily by Scottish Presbyterian and English Anglican settlers from the 17th century onward. Billy parish sits in this predominantly Protestant, Ulster-Scots belt.
- **Religious denominations present:** Church of Ireland (Anglican/Episcopal), Presbyterian (several congregations), Roman Catholic, and potentially smaller nonconformist groups (Methodist, Baptist)

## Boundary and jurisdictional context

Billy is an ancient Church of Ireland civil parish. Throughout 1780–1870 it remained within County Antrim, which itself remained a consistent county-level jurisdiction throughout the period. No boundary split affecting Billy is indicated by the tools. In 1921, the Government of Ireland Act took effect and County Antrim (along with five other Ulster counties) remained in the United Kingdom as part of Northern Ireland; this has significant consequences for where records are held today (see below), but is outside the 1780–1870 target window and affects only record custody, not record creation.

The 1922 fire at the Public Record Office of Ireland (PROI) in Dublin — which occurred after Irish partition — destroyed large quantities of records that had been centrally deposited, including many Church of Ireland registers that had been required by law to be deposited there. This is the single most important event shaping record survival for this parish. The FamilySearch Wiki page for [Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records) states plainly that "Church of Ireland (Anglican, Episcopalian) records began in 1536, but two-thirds were destroyed in 1922."

**Because County Antrim is in Northern Ireland**, the primary repository for surviving original records is the **Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI)** in Belfast, not the National Archives in Dublin. The two national archives hold overlapping copies of some national-level records (civil registration, census) up to 1922, per the Ireland Church Records wiki page.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)

- **Start date:** Civil registration of all births, marriages, and deaths in Ireland began at the **national (all-Ireland) level in 1864**, per the Ireland Church Records wiki page's statement that "before civil registration was introduced in 1864, Church records provide the primary source for providing baptism, marriage and burial dates." Non-Catholic marriages only had been registered since 1845. The FamilySearch Wiki did not return a dedicated `Ireland_Vital_Records` page — the wiki_read server returned a generic fallback for that URL.
- **What this means for 1780–1870:** Civil registration covers only 1864–1870 within the target window (births, marriages, deaths). All events before 1864 require church records as the primary source. Non-Catholic marriages are registered from 1845.
- **Where held:** The General Register Office Northern Ireland (GRONI) holds civil registration records for the Northern Ireland counties. Copies of records up to 1922 may also be held at the General Register Office in Dublin (for the Republic). GRONI's records are accessible through IrishGenealogy.ie and through PRONI.
- **Online access:** [IrishGenealogy.ie](https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/en/) is named in the Ireland Church Records wiki page as an online portal; note the page states it currently covers County Kerry, western/northwestern County Cork, and most of the City of Dublin — it does not list County Antrim coverage. The [Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes, 1623–1866](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3460239) at FamilySearch (index and images, free) covers pre-civil-registration marriages and is relevant to the 1780–1864 gap. This collection is also at MyHeritage and FindMyPast (subscription).
- **Gaps:** No civil births, marriages, or deaths exist before 1864 (except non-Catholic marriages from 1845). The 1922 PROI fire destroyed many pre-1922 centrally deposited records.

### Church records

This is the most critical record class for 1780–1864. The Ireland Church Records wiki page ([https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records)) provides the following grounded findings:

**Church of Ireland (Anglican/Episcopal) — the directly asked question**

The wiki page states that Church of Ireland records "began in 1536, but two-thirds were destroyed in 1922." This refers to the destruction of registers that had been deposited at the Dublin PROI. The surviving third — and registers that were never deposited or were copied before the fire — are held at two institutions named in the wiki page:

- **PRONI (Belfast):** [PRONI's Guide to Church Records](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf) — this guide, cited in the wiki page, "will help you identify what churches exist in each parish, what records exist for each church and whether the records are available in PRONI, either on microfilm or in original form. The majority of parishes covered in the Guide are located within the six counties of Northern Ireland." Because Billy civil parish is in County Antrim (Northern Ireland), PRONI is the first place to check for surviving Church of Ireland registers. The wiki page also notes [Digitised Church Records Available in PRONI](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni#toc-1).
- **RCB Library (Dublin):** The Representative Church Body Library at Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14 (library@ireland.anglican.org) holds surviving Church of Ireland registers not at PRONI. The wiki page links to [their List of Parish Registers](https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf) and a [Request a Search](https://store.ireland.anglican.org/genealogy) service. The RCB Library should be checked alongside PRONI.
- **FindMyPast (subscription):** The wiki page lists the [Irish Parish Register Baptisms & Confirmations, Ffolliott Collection](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/irish-parish-register-baptisms-and-confirmations-ffolliott-collection), [Irish Parish Register Marriages, Ffolliott Collection](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/irish-parish-register-marriages-ffolliott-collection), and [Irish Parish Register Burials, Ffolliott Collection](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/irish-parish-register-burials-ffolliott-collection) — these are indexes to Church of Ireland (Anglican) parish registers compiled by Ffolliott, available at FindMyPast.
- **Ancestry (subscription):** [Ireland, Abstracts of Wills and Marriages, 1620–1923](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/62059) — index only.

The specific fate of Billy parish's own Church of Ireland registers is not confirmed by any tool result in this run. To determine whether the Billy parish registers survived 1922, the researcher must consult PRONI's Guide to Church Records and the RCB Library's parish register list, both linked above.

**Roman Catholic records**

The wiki page states that Catholic records "began from the mid-1700s. Most rural parishes did not start keeping records until Catholic Emancipation in 1828. Many of the city registers date from the 1750s." For a rural parish like Billy in 1780, Catholic registers may not begin until close to 1828 or later. The Catholic ecclesiastical parish (which does not necessarily align with the civil parish boundaries) would be the holder.

Online access named in the wiki page:

- [Catholic Records, National Library of Ireland](https://registers.nli.ie/) — free online
- [Ireland Roman Catholic Parish Marriages](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/ireland-roman-catholic-parish-marriages) at FindMyPast (subscription)
- [Ireland, Catholic Qualification & Convert Rolls, 1701–1845](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3499248) at FamilySearch — free, index and images

**Presbyterian records**

The wiki page states: "In 1605 Scottish estate owners resettled mostly Presbyterian tenants from their estates to newly established estates in Northern Ireland. Numerous registers date from the 1600s, but the average starting date for these registers is 1830." Given the strong Ulster-Scots settlement in the Bushmills area, Presbyterian registers are highly likely to be relevant. However, the 1830 average start date means the 1780–1829 window may have limited Presbyterian coverage for many congregations.

Online resources named in the wiki page:
- [Ireland, Non-Conformist Births & Baptisms](http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-births-and-baptisms) at FindMyPast (subscription)
- [Ireland, Non-Conformist Marriages](http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-marriages) at FindMyPast (subscription)
- [Ireland, Non-Conformist Burials](http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-burials) at FindMyPast (subscription)
- [Ulster Historical Foundation](http://www.ancestryireland.com/) — relevant for Ulster Presbyterian research

**Important note on Catholic vs. Church of Ireland parish boundaries:** The wiki page advises to "search surrounding localities if you cannot find records in the expected locality. Catholics had different parish boundaries to the Church of Ireland." The Catholic ecclesiastical parish covering the Bushmills area may not correspond in name or extent to the Billy civil parish; the researcher should verify which Catholic parish serves the townlands of interest.

**Burial registers:** The wiki page notes that "Catholic and Presbyterian church registers frequently do not contain burial registers." For those denominations, church-held burial records should not be assumed to exist; cemetery inscriptions are the main alternative.

### Census records

The volume_search and collections_search tools returned no results for this place (the place tools failed to resolve the standardPlace). Based on the Ireland Church Records wiki page's historical background, Ireland was enumerated in national censuses by the British government:

- 1901 and 1911 Irish census returns survive and are widely available online (outside the target window but useful for backward reconstruction)
- The 1821, 1831, 1841, and 1851 census returns for most of Ireland were destroyed — some in the PROI fire of 1922 and some earlier. The 1861 and 1871 returns were destroyed by government order shortly after enumeration. The 1881 and 1891 returns were pulped during World War I.
- **Within the 1780–1870 window, no surviving national census enumerations are known to exist for County Antrim.** The wiki page does not contradict this well-established fact, but it also does not state it directly — no Ireland_Census page was successfully returned by the tools.
- Substitute census-type records for the pre-1864 window include the Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837) and Griffith's Valuation (1847–1864), discussed under Tax/Land records below.

### Probate and court records

- No Ireland_Probate page was successfully returned by the tools.
- The wiki page for Ireland Church Records names the [Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes, 1623–1866](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3460239) and [Index to Prerogative marriage license bonds, ca. 1750–1849](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/117060) — these are relevant to confirming marriages among more affluent families.
- The wiki page also lists [Ireland, Indexes to Wills, Probate Administration, Marriage Bonds and Licences, 1591–1866](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/62077/) at Ancestry (index and images, subscription) — this covers wills and administrations during the target period.
- Probate before 1858 was handled by the ecclesiastical (prerogative and diocesan) courts; from 1858 by civil district probate registries. County Antrim falls in the diocese of Connor and Down, and the prerogative court of Armagh handled higher-value estates.
- The 1922 PROI fire destroyed most original pre-1858 wills and administrations deposited in Dublin. Indexes, abstracts, and copies survive in various collections. Key substitute resources named in the wiki page:
  - [Betham Genealogical Abstracts](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/betham-genealogical-abstracts) at FindMyPast — "abstracts of genealogical records collected by Sir William Betham. Useful substitute to records lost in the 1922 Public Record Office fire in Dublin."
  - [Crossle Genealogical Abstracts](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/crossle-genealogical-abstracts) at FindMyPast
  - [Thrift Genealogical Abstracts](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/thrift-genealogical-abstracts) at FindMyPast — "abstracts of genealogical records including wills, parish registers, freeman lists, and pedigree charts. Records date as far back as the 16th century."

### Land records

- No Ireland_Land_and_Property page was successfully returned by the tools; the relevant wiki_read returned only a generic fallback.

  - **Griffith's Primary Valuation (1847–1864):** A systematic survey of all landholders and occupiers in Ireland. County Antrim was covered. This is the single most important mid-century land/population record. Griffith's Valuation is searchable at [AskAboutIreland.ie](https://www.askaboutireland.ie/griffith-valuation/) (free) and also at Ancestry and other databases.
- Land title registration and deed records are held at the Registry of Deeds, Dublin (deeds from 1708) and at PRONI for Northern Ireland properties. PRONI holds estate papers, rentals, and leases for many County Antrim landed estates, which can document tenants across the period.
- The FamilySearch Wiki returned no specific data on land-distribution jurisdiction for this area; the tool data is insufficient to name the specific land office or granting authority beyond the general statements above.

### Immigration and emigration records

- **Flax growers' lists (1796)** — some are online but coverage should be verified at PRONI/local heritage centres
- **Freeholder and voter lists** — partially available but comprehensiveness is not confirmed by tools

## Known record losses

The FamilySearch Wiki page for [Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records) states that "Church of Ireland (Anglican, Episcopalian) records began in 1536, but **two-thirds were destroyed in 1922**." This refers to the fire at the Public Record Office of Ireland in Dublin, where Church of Ireland registers had been required to be deposited. The same page identifies the Betham, Crossle, and Thrift genealogical abstracts as "useful substitutes to records lost in the 1922 Public Record Office fire in Dublin."

Whether the Church of Ireland registers for **Billy parish specifically** were among the destroyed two-thirds, or among the surviving third, is not confirmed by any tool result in this survey. The researcher must check:
1. PRONI's Guide to Church Records (linked above) — this will state whether Billy parish registers are held at PRONI and their date range
2. The RCB Library's List of Parish Registers — this will show registers held in Dublin

The 1922 fire also destroyed most original pre-1858 wills and administration bonds deposited at the PROI. Indexes and abstracts (Betham, Thrift, Crossle) partially compensate. Most Irish national census returns for the 1820s–1880s were destroyed either in 1922 or by government action. No surviving enumeration covers County Antrim within the 1780–1870 window.

## Research tips

- **Start with the PRONI Guide to Church Records** ([PDF](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf)) to establish exactly which Church of Ireland, Presbyterian, and Catholic registers survive for Billy civil parish and the congregations within it, and whether they are on microfilm or original form at PRONI. This is the single most important first step. Source: [Ireland Church Records — FamilySearch Wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records).
- **Search Church of Ireland records even if your family was not Anglican.** The wiki page advises: "Search available Church of Ireland records even if your family was not of the Church of Ireland." Church of Ireland registers were sometimes the most consistently kept in a given locality.
- **Catholic and Church of Ireland parish boundaries differ.** The Catholic ecclesiastical parish serving the Bushmills area does not necessarily match Billy civil parish boundaries. Verify which Catholic parish covers the townland you are researching. Source: [Ireland Church Records — FamilySearch Wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records).
- **Catholic registers for rural parishes may not begin before 1828.** The wiki page states that "most rural parishes did not start keeping records until Catholic Emancipation in 1828." For 1780–1828, Church of Ireland and Presbyterian registers may be the only surviving church records. Source: [Ireland Church Records — FamilySearch Wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records).
- **Presbyterian average start date is 1830.** The wiki page states "the average starting date for these registers is 1830." Individual congregations vary; some Antrim Presbyterian registers are earlier, but this is the realistic average. Source: [Ireland Church Records — FamilySearch Wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records).
- **Griffith's Valuation (1847–1864) and the Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837) are the census substitutes for this period.** They list every landholder/occupier at townland level and are the closest equivalent to a mid-century census for Billy parish. Search AskAboutIreland.ie and IrishGenealogy.ie for free access.
- **Identify the specific townland.** Irish records are organised at the townland level, below the civil parish. Knowing the townland dramatically narrows the search in registers, valuations, and estate papers. Use Samuel Lewis's *Topographical Dictionary of Ireland* (1837) or the Ordnance Survey memoirs of the 1830s for place identification in Billy parish.
- **The Ulster Historical Foundation** ([ancestryireland.com](http://www.ancestryireland.com/)) specialises in Ulster-Scots and Northern Ireland research and may hold transcripts and indexes not available elsewhere. Source: [Ireland Church Records — FamilySearch Wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records).
- **Genealogical abstracts compensate for 1922 losses.** The Betham, Thrift, and Crossle abstracts (all at FindMyPast) cover wills, parish registers, and other records, some of which were destroyed in 1922. These are not complete substitutes but name individuals who appear in no surviving original. Source: [Ireland Church Records — FamilySearch Wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records).
- **Search both PRONI and the RCB Library for Church of Ireland registers.** Registers for a single Church of Ireland parish can be split between Belfast and Dublin depending on when and whether they were deposited. The researcher should check both institutions' finding aids before concluding a register is lost.
- **Cross-border research:** Billy parish is in County Antrim, not near a county or national boundary within the target period, so cross-border complexity is lower than for border parishes. However, the Presbyterian congregational network spans north Antrim and east Londonderry (Derry), and some families' baptismal or marriage records may be in registers of congregations in the Route or Bann valley area.

This survey covers Billy civil parish, County Antrim, for 1780–1870. Because County Antrim is in Northern Ireland, the two repositories that matter most for this period are PRONI in Belfast and the RCB Library in Dublin — PRONI for surviving registers and estate papers, the RCB Library for Church of Ireland registers that were not at PRONI. output.text_response:
# Locality Guide: Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania (1840s–1860s)

## Jurisdiction Overview

- **Formed:** 1811, from parts of Berks and Northampton counties
- **County seat:** Pottsville
- **Economy:** Dominated by the anthracite coal industry — one of the most productive regions in the U.S. Mining, ironworking, and canal/rail transport were all active.
- **Ethnic composition:** Large waves of Welsh, Irish, German, and English immigrants drawn by the coal industry. German-speaking settlers were numerous enough that some church records were kept in both English and German.
- **Denominations present:** Lutheran, Catholic (Irish immigrants), Methodist, Welsh Calvinist Methodist, and other Protestant congregations.

---

## Available Record Types

### Census Records *(Most Accessible Online)*
- **1850 and 1860 Federal Census** — FamilySearch has 1 digitized volume (image group 007621224, 412 images), **96% name-indexed and full-text searchable**. This is the most accessible digitized record set for this place and period.
- **1850 and 1860 Mortality Schedules** — Record deaths in the year preceding each census; key substitutes for missing death records.
- **1840 Census** — Available in the national census collection.
- Also searchable on Ancestry: https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1276/

### Vital Records *(Church Records Are the Key Source)*
- Pennsylvania did **not require statewide civil registration until 1906**. Vital events in the 1840s–1860s were recorded almost exclusively in **church registers**, not government offices.
- **Lutheran church records** — FamilySearch has 1 digitized volume (image group 004288771, 198 images, 1840–1875). However, it is **0% name-indexed** (browse-only) and **not full-text searchable**, and is written in **both English and German** (Kurrent/Sütterlin script). This must be browsed page by page.
- Other denominations (Catholic, Methodist, Welsh Calvinist) are not yet in digitized FamilySearch volumes — physical repositories only.

### Probate Records
- FamilySearch has 1 digitized volume (image group 004812990, 286 images, 1845–1880), only **4% name-indexed** but **full-text searchable**.
- Also part of the larger "Pennsylvania, Probate Records, 1683–1994" collection (3,200,560 images, no name index — image browse only).
- **Originals held at:** Schuylkill County Courthouse (Register of Wills and Orphans' Court), Pottsville.

### Land Records
- Pennsylvania is a **state-land state** — original grants came from the Commonwealth, not the federal BLM.
- Deed books for the 1840s–1860s are held at the **Schuylkill County Recorder of Deeds**, Pottsville; warrants and patents at the **Pennsylvania State Archives**, Harrisburg.
- **No digitized land record volumes for this period were found** — physical or microfilm access required.

### Military Records
- Relevant conflicts: **Mexican-American War (1846–1848)** and **Civil War (1861–1865)**.
- Types: service records, pension files, bounty land warrants, Civil War muster rolls, 1863 draft registration records.
- **Held at:** NARA (federal records); Pennsylvania State Archives (state military records and Veterans' File).
- No Schuylkill County–specific digitized military volumes were found.

### Naturalization Records
- Pre-1906, **any court of record** could naturalize immigrants — including the Schuylkill County Court of Common Pleas.
- Search county court minutes and naturalization dockets at the courthouse, not only federal records.

### Immigration / Passenger Records
- **Primary port of entry:** Philadelphia; secondary port for Germans: Baltimore.
- Passenger lists are available on Ancestry and FamilySearch at the national level.
- No county-specific immigration volumes found.

### Tax Records
- County property and personal property tax assessments exist from 1811 onward.
- Held at the **Pennsylvania State Archives** and **Schuylkill County Historical Society**.
- No digitized tax volumes for 1840–1870 found — useful as a between-census substitute.

### Cemetery Records
- **FindAGrave** (https://www.findagrave.com) and **BillionGraves** host volunteer-transcribed headstone records — search these directly.
- Physical sexton/burial records held by individual congregations or denominational archives.

### Newspapers
- **The Miners' Journal** (Pottsville) is a major source for obituaries, legal notices, marriage announcements, and estate settlements.
- Held on microfilm at the **Pottsville Free Public Library** and **Schuylkill County Historical Society**.
- Check **Chronicling America** (https://chroniclingamerica.loc.gov) for possible partial coverage.

### Mining / Occupational Records
- Employment rolls, mine accident reports, and company store ledgers can document a miner's presence in years with no other surviving record.
- Held at the **Pennsylvania State Archives** and local historical societies — not online.

---

## Repository Guide

### Online

| Repository | Holdings | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | 1850–1860 Census (96% indexed); Lutheran Church Records 1840–1875 (browse-only, English/German); Probate Records 1845–1880 (full-text searchable); Pennsylvania Probate Records 1683–1994 (image-only, 3.2M images) | Free |
| Ancestry | 1850 US Federal Census – Schuylkill County | Subscription |

### Physical Repositories

| Repository | Holdings |
